headline: Google indexed the first URL this project has ever had, and two money-path defects were found and fixed: hosted buyers were losing their data, and crawlers were having live Stripe sessions created for them.

google.caveat: 140 of 141 remain uncrawled and impressions are still zero. Googlebot made exactly one sitemap fetch in 24.7 hours.
google.artefact_caught: the discovered/unknown coverage split is not trackable: two censuses 15 minutes apart disagreed on 82 of 141 URLs, so only in-index and ever-crawled are reportable

registry_referrals.verdict: flat, and exactly flat: every count byte-identical to the baseline, and zero registry-referred requests in the 24.7 hours since
registry_referrals.fair_caveat: four of the five changes had been live for 1.4 to 2.6 hours at window close, so this measures deployment, not effect. The recorded criterion says re-run on or after 2026-09-15.

human_traffic_corrected.was: 137 off-homepage page views on a render-proof filter
human_traffic_corrected.why: one user-agent string touched 53 of 141 pages from eight countries, and 18 of 53 render-proven agents appeared from more than one country. A rendering crawler fetches assets too, so an asset fetch proves a browser engine, not a person.

defects_fixed.hosted_buyers_lost_their_data: On the hosted endpoints the tenant IS the token, so a buyer who reconnected with their licence key landed on a different tenant and left their invoices behind. license_activate was a stub whose description even contradicted its own schema. It now binds a verified key to the caller's own anonymous token, using the same mechanism a hosted purchase already used. Verified live: free to pro on the same token with the invoice intact; a garbage key and a valid key for another product both change nothing.
defects_fixed.crawlers_created_live_stripe_sessions: A crawler sending a browser-shaped user agent with accept */* had a real cs_live_ checkout session created for it, while python-requests was correctly turned away. That put a Stripe call on the critical path of requests nobody would pay for, which is the likely cause of 691 gateway timeouts on /buy/* in 25 hours, every one with no recognisable browser, and it inflated the human-checkout-sessions figure. A navigation signal is now required of every request.
defects_fixed.hosted_path_was_invisible: The zero-install hosted URL sat at character 20,676 of a 21,905-character product page while the page led with the price. It now sits at character 153 on all 30 hosted servers, driven by a list derived from the manifests behind a drift test that was control-tested.

inbound_links: 18 of 18 still live, including all four placed on 2026-09-08. The two lost earlier are still lost. One remains fragile because it was shipped by a live-mirror deploy against a repo that is behind live.

honesty_gates.problem: billing/ is not an npm workspace, so root npm test never ran its tests. Six assertions were red at HEAD for days, including the gate written to stop the home page restating a stale check count, which had itself gone stale.
honesty_gates.resolved: 107 of 107, and the directory is now discovered and run by scripts/release-check.mjs, which walks the tree rather than holding a list so a new test directory cannot be born outside every gate. Control-tested by breaking an assertion and watching the gate catch it.
honesty_gates.worst_case: data/tests.json said 1,507 unit tests and the real figure is 1,563. README renders that file and build-readme --check gates the README against it, so a green gate was hiding a stale public number. Corrected.
honesty_gates.live_defect_found: a guide promising every figure came from a specific run was quoting today's bundle instead: 31 servers and 292 tools where that run produced 24 and 224. Corrected to the run's own numbers.
honesty_gates.also_found: office-suite was emitted twice in llms.txt under two titles for one URL, 34 product lines for a 32-product catalogue, in the file assistant crawlers actually read

novel_findings_published: a capital letter in a GitHub username is worth about 20 places in registry search order, proved against live data and the registry's own source
the registry enforces one hosted URL per server name, quoted from validateNoDuplicateRemoteURLs, which is undocumented on its publishing pages
25.4 percent of 16,305 listed remote MCP endpoints require auth on the discovery methods directories probe, so the 401 trap is an ecosystem-wide problem

estate.billing_gates: 107 of 107, and the gate caught my own stale figure within the hour: re-running validation moved the median and the home page still restated the old one

mirrors.synced: 32 of 32, none failed or skipped, and mcp-delivery-schedule created so the 32-servers-31-mirrors gap is closed
mirrors.ci: 32 of 32 green after the livelock fix was synced out
mirrors.dockerfiles: 0 of 32 still ship the file that could not build, from 30 of 31
mirrors.generator_defects: the agent ran every generated tree locally before pushing and found four defects in its own generator; without that pre-flight 9 of 32 mirrors would have gone red

livelock.what: a caller-supplied out_path under /proc, /sys or /dev hung the server permanently
livelock.cause: mkdirSync with recursive never returns on a pseudo-filesystem: mkdir answers ENOENT in 0 ms, Node reads that as a missing parent and retries forever. Reproduced in a node:22-alpine container where it had not returned after 25 seconds.
livelock.scope: seven servers, not the one whose test caught it: timezone, calendar, clauses, docx, resume, spreadsheet, zip
livelock.fix: a bounded ancestor walk creating each level non-recursively. Verified on Linux: /proc throws ENOENT and /sys throws EROFS, both in 0 ms, and a normal nested path still succeeds
livelock.my_error: I first made the failing test avoid /proc, which turned the suite green while the defect stayed shipped. The mirror agent refused to hide it, which is how it was found.
